title: Administrator
description:

This is a varied and busy role where no two days are necessarily the same.

What will you be doing?

- Coordinating travel arrangements and bookings.
- Providing general administrative and office support.
- Keeping records and information organised and up to date.

- Confident managing appointments, diaries and travel arrangements.

title: Credit Controllers
description:
Our accountancy and finance recruitment team is partnering with an established multi-site services organisation based in Southampton. With a diverse customer base and a collaborative culture, the business is seeking a Credit Controller to join its finance team on a temporary basis. The role offers hybrid working, varied responsibilities and the opportunity to contribute to an important area of the organisation s financial operations.

What will the Credit Controller role involve?
- Support the finance team with the effective management of customer accounts across business and individual customers
- Maintain regular contact with customers by telephone, email and written correspondence to encourage prompt payment
- Work closely with operational teams to investigate account queries and help resolve outstanding balances

Suitable Candidate for the Credit Controller vacancy:
- Previous experience in credit control, customer service, accounts administration or a similar environment
- Confident communicator who can handle payment discussions professionally and sensitively
- Organised, attentive to detail and comfortable managing varied customer accounts

Additional benefits and information for the role of Credit Controller:
- Immediate start
- Hybrid working, with two days per week from home
- Free parking

title: Customer Administrator
description:
Job Title: Customer Administrator

Location: Southampton
Contract Type: Temporary
Industry: Logistics & Transportation

Are you ready to embark on a vibrant journey in the logistics and transportation sector? Our client, a leading organisation in the industry, is seeking enthusiastic and detail-oriented Customer Administrators to join their dynamic team on a temporary basis. This is an exciting opportunity for individuals who thrive in a fast-paced environment and are passionate about delivering exceptional customer service.

Key Responsibilities:
- Provide outstanding administrative support to the customer service team.
- Handle customer inquiries via phone, email, and in-person with professionalism and a friendly attitude.
- Process orders, manage shipments, and track deliveries to ensure customer satisfaction.
- Collaborate with various departments to resolve customer issues and enhance service delivery.
- Maintain accurate records and databases to support efficient operations.
- Assist in the preparation of reports and documentation as needed.

What Makes This Role Exciting:
- Engage with a diverse clientele and be the face of the organisation.
- Contribute to a positive team environment where your ideas and input are valued.
- Gain hands-on experience in the logistics and transportation industry, enhancing your professional skill set.
- Work in a supportive and lively atmosphere that encourages growth and development.

Ideal Candidate Profile:
- Previous experience in customer service or administration, preferably within logistics or transportation.
- Strong communication skills, both verbal and written, with a keen attention to detail.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and experience with customer management systems.
- Ability to multitask and prioritise effectively in a busy environment.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and a customer-first mindset.

Why Choose This Opportunity?
- Competitive pay rates that recognise your skills and contributions.
- Flexible working hours to accommodate your lifestyle.
- A chance to make a real impact in an organisation that values its employees.
- Opportunities for professional development and potential future roles within the company.

How to Apply:
If this vibrant opportunity aligns with your career aspirations, don't hesitate! Our client is eager to meet motivated individuals ready to make a difference. Please submit your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

Join our client in delivering excellence in customer service within the logistics and transportation industry! This is more than just a job; it's a chance to grow and shine in a supportive environment. Take the next step in your career today!

Our client is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals.

title: Document Controller
company: Tilbury Douglas Construction Ltd - Company - Permanent
description:
Document Controller

Location: Southampton

We are looking to appoint a detail-oriented and highly organised Document Controller to join our team. This is a key role responsible for managing and controlling project documentation, ensuring information is accurately maintained, distributed, and stored in line with company procedures and project requirements.

Working closely with project teams, consultants, subcontractors, and stakeholders, you will support the efficient flow of information across projects, maintain document control systems, and provide expertise in the use of Common Data Environment (CDE) platforms. You will play an important role in ensuring project teams have access to accurate, up-to-date documentation while promoting best practice in information management.

Key Duties
- Manage and control project document flow, ensuring all project documentation is accurate, current, and distributed to relevant stakeholders
- Provide guidance, training, and support to project teams and subcontractors on document control procedures and Common Data Environment (CDE) systems
- Maintain document control systems, business archives, and information management processes, ensuring records are securely stored and easily accessible
- Support project and design teams by monitoring documentation, resolving document control issues, and providing regular reporting when required
- Ensure confidentiality of sensitive information while delivering administrative support and identifying opportunities for process improvement

About You

You will be a proactive and organised professional with strong administration skills and experience managing project documentation within a construction or project-based environment.

You will bring:
- Previous experience in a Document Controller role, with knowledge of document management processes and procedures
- Experience using Common Data Environment (CDE) platforms and document control systems such as ASITE, BIW, 4 Projects, or similar
- Strong administration, organisational, and Microsoft Office skills, with excellent attention to detail
- Basic understanding of BIM and the ability to work collaboratively with project teams and stakeholders
- GCSEs/A Levels (or equivalent), NVQ in IT/Administration or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience

What We Can Offer You
- Competitive salary and car allowance 26 days annual leave, with the option to buy or sell up to 3 days
- Additional long service leave at 3, 7, and 10 years
- Private medical insurance (with option to extend to family)
- Life assurance and pension matched up to 8%
- Enhanced family leave policies
- 2 volunteering days per year
- Flexible and agile working (role dependent)
- Employee Assistance Programme and Perks at Work discount platform
- Flexible benefits including critical illness cover, dental insurance, travel insurance, cycle to work scheme, and retail vouchers

Who We Are

Tilbury Douglas is a leading UK building, infrastructure, engineering and fit-out company delivering vital projects across sectors including health, education, highways, justice, defence, aviation, water, and environment.

Our people are at the heart of our success. We are committed to creating an inclusive culture that encourages innovation, values individual differences, and supports professional development. We are proud to have retained our Investors in Diversity Silver Award.

We look forward to receiving your application.

title: Operations Support Coordinator
description:
- Operations Support Coordinator
- Southampton, Hampshire
- 6-month contract
- £32,000 to £35,000 per year (Pro-Rata)

Summary:

Our client is looking for an experienced, organised Operations Support Coordinator to support its UK operations team based in Southampton, working within roadside technology and traffic safety.

You will coordinate operational administration and customer reporting, while ensuring invoices, purchase orders and supporting records are accurate and processed on time.

Working closely with the Operations Manager, field engineers and contractors, you will help keep maintenance activities and customer projects running smoothly.

This position would suit someone comfortable managing competing deadlines, investigating discrepancies and following actions through to completion within a technical service environment.

Role and Responsibilities:
- Process monthly customer invoices, checking contract requirements, supporting documentation, purchase order references and internal approvals.
- Raise, track and reconcile purchase orders for equipment, contractor services and project materials.
- Prepare customer performance reports covering service levels, KPIs, maintenance activity and contractual reporting requirements.
- Coordinate work permits, site access and contractor inductions to support planned field activities.
- Maintain accurate operational registers, compliance records, project trackers and asset information.
- Manage customer support inboxes, prioritising requests, tracking responses and escalating outstanding issues.
- Analyse service and maintenance data to identify recurring problems, reporting discrepancies and opportunities for improvement.
- Maintain meeting actions, controlled documents and audit evidence, following up with relevant colleagues and contractors.

Skills and Experience:
- At least three years experience in business administration, operations support or a closely related position.
- Experience supporting technicians or maintenance teams within a technical, regulated environment.
- Practical experience processing invoices and purchase orders using an ERP system; SAP Business ByDesign experience is desirable.
- Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, with confidence maintaining spreadsheets and checking data accuracy.
- Experience gathering and analysing operational information to produce clear customer and senior management reports.
- Foundational project support skills, including scheduling, documentation, action tracking and coordination.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to manage customer queries and obtain information from busy operational teams.
- A careful, structured approach to managing deadlines, resolving discrepancies and maintaining auditable records.
- A Level 3 or Level 4 business administration qualification, or equivalent, is desirable.

Applications:

To learn more about our client and this opportunity working as an Operations Support Coordinator based in Southampton, please call James Sample or send your CV for more information.

Please contact James here at ISR in our Transport Technology team to learn more about how you can become a part of our client s ongoing success. This is fantastic opportunity to work for a genuine industry leader who are shaping how we use day-to-day services in the modern world.

title: People Assistant
description:
Liberty Recruitment Group are delighted to be working exclusively with a fantastic, well-established organisation in the search for a People Assistant to join their friendly and supportive HR team.

This is a brilliant opportunity for someone looking to start their career in HR, or perhaps someone with a little HR administration experience who is keen to develop their knowledge within a collaborative and people-focused environment.

Based in Southampton or Salisbury, this is a full-time, permanent and office-based role, offering a salary of circa £25,000, depending on experience.

Key responsibilities:
- Coordinate new starter processes, including preparing welcome packs, employment documentation and delivering inductions
- Manage leaver administration, including relevant paperwork and reference requests
- Record and update absence, annual leave, flexi-time and employee benefits information
- Support the coordination of training, CPD and wider learning and development activities
- Support the recruitment team with interview coordination, CV screening and candidate administration when required
- Coordinate work experience placements and support wider employee initiatives
- Respond to employee queries, providing a friendly and professional service
- Assist with HR compliance activity, including DBS checks and GDPR requirements
- Organise regular team review meetings and provide general administrative support to the wider HR team

About you
- Previous administration experience would be advantageous, although not essential
- A genuine interest in HR and developing a career within People & Culture
- A naturally people-focused approach with strong emotional intelligence
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Professional, approachable and confident communicating with people at all levels
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office
- Full UK driving licence, as occasional travel between offices will be required

If you're looking to take your first steps into HR, or build on your existing experience within a supportive and friendly team, we would love to hear from you!

Please get in touch with the team at Liberty Recruitment Group to find out more.

title: Placement Coordinator - Quality and Integration
description:
Placement Coordinator - Quality and Integration

Location: Southampton
Employer: Southampton City Council
Job Type: temporary contract on going
Salary: 14.92 per/hour
DBS Requirement: Enhanced DBS

About the Role

Southampton City Council is seeking an organised, proactive and customer-focused Placement Coordinator to join its Quality and Integration team.

The successful candidate will provide essential administrative and coordination support to Adult and Children's Social Care teams, working closely with healthcare partners and service providers to arrange appropriate care packages and placements for vulnerable adults and children.

This is an important role within the Placement Service, ensuring that suitable support arrangements are sourced efficiently, contracts are accurately prepared and providers are paid within agreed timescales.

Key Responsibilities
- Receive referrals from social care practitioners and arrange appropriate care packages and placements.
- Liaise with social workers, healthcare professionals, service providers, commissioners and finance teams.
- Create, amend and maintain individual placement contracts and agreements accurately.
- Ensure providers receive the correct contractual information to enable timely payments.
- Respond to queries and resolve issues relating to care arrangements and payments.
- Maintain accurate records and update the relevant social care systems, including PARIS.
- Monitor service availability and occupancy levels to support effective placement sourcing.
- Identify gaps in the provider market and report trends to management.
- Prepare information and reports to support the effective management of the service.
- Maintain confidentiality and ensure compliance with council policies and procedures.

Essential Skills and Experience

The ideal candidate will have:
- Excellent communication and customer service skills, with the ability to deal professionally and sensitively with confidential information.
- Experience liaising with different professionals, service providers and external organisations.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- Good problem-solving skills and the ability to work efficiently under pressure.
- Accurate data entry and keyboard skills.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel.
- The ability to work independently and as part of a team.
- A flexible and proactive approach, with the ability to provide cover for colleagues when required.
- An understanding of confidentiality, equality, diversity and data protection.

Desirable Experience
- Previous experience in a social care, healthcare, placements, commissioning or administrative environment.
- Knowledge of care packages, placement arrangements and provider contracts.
- Experience using PARIS or similar social care recording systems.

Personal Attributes

We are looking for someone who is:
- Professional, approachable and customer-focused.
- Reliable, organised and highly detail-oriented.
- A confident communicator who can build positive working relationships.
- Collaborative and supportive of colleagues.
- Adaptable, proactive and committed to continuous improvement.

Additional Information

The successful candidate will be required to undergo an Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check.

How to Apply

If you have strong administrative and coordination skills, enjoy working with a range of professionals and are passionate about supporting services for vulnerable adults and children, we would welcome your application.

Please submit your CV for consideration.

We are committed to fair and inclusive recruitment. All applicants will be considered on the basis of their skills, experience, qualifications and ability to perform the role, and no applicant will be treated less favourably because of a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010.

title: Administrator
company: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: Make a Difference Every Day Are you an organised, proactive administrator looking for a rewarding role where your work truly matters? We are recruiting for a full time Administrator (Mon to Fri 09:00-17:00) to join our friendly, supportive Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) based at College Keep. Our service provides specialist secondary mental health care for adults aged 18-65 living with severe and enduring mental health conditions. As a member of our established admin team, you will play a vital role in supporting clinicians, consultants, service users and carers, ensuring the smooth running of a busy, compassionate service. At Central CMHT, we are committed to creating an inclusive, supportive workplace where staff wellbeing is a priority. You will join a welcoming team that values collaboration, development and continuous learning. This is an opportunity to build a rewarding career and make a genuine difference to the lives of people accessing mental health services. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy helping people, can remain calm and organised, we'd love to hear from you. What You'll Be Doing: As the first point of contact for many of our service users, you'll provide a professional, welcoming and supportive service while delivering essential administrative support to the wider clinical team. Key responsibilities include: Acting as the first point of contact for service users, carers and professionals Managing high volumes of telephone calls and enquiries Monitoring and responding to incoming emails Carrying out reception duties as required Processing referrals accurately and efficiently Booking and amending appointments Preparing and typing clinical correspondence Preparing agendas and taking meeting minutes Maintaining accurate records on our electronic patient record system (RIO) Providing administrative support to clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team We're looking for someone who is: Enthusiastic, motivated and highly organised Able to work effectively in a busy environment with changing priorities A strong team player with a positive, can-do attitude Professional, compassionate and able to communicate confidently with a wide range of people Comfortable handling sensitive and confidential information Detail-focused with excellent administration skills Confident using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook - training will be provided for our electronic patient record system, RIO. Able to maintain accurate records and demonstrate good literacy and numeracy skills Further information about the Trust and this role can be found on the Job Description and Person Specification document attached. title: Dental Receptionist
company: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: Are you an enthusiastic, flexible, reliable team player with excellent communication skills? HIOWH Special Care Dental Service is looking to recruit a Dental Receptionists to work within the Special Care Dental clinics situated in Pickles Coppice Millbrook in Southampton. Our service delivers routine and urgent care to patients, adults and children who are unable to access care in the General Dental Services due to their additional needs. This includes adults and children with a physical, sensory, intellectual, mental, medical, social impairment or disability and individuals with behavioural difficulties or dental anxiety. You will provide reception and administrative support to the whole dental team, providing an efficient effective service for our special care patients. There will be a need for you to provide cover as and when needed at the other clinics with the possibility for travel over the wider area of Hampshire. You will be confident, able to work under pressure with the ability to communicate effectively, delivering care with dignity and respect in a kind compassionate manner. It is important that applicants can demonstrate strong interpersonal, communication skills, excellent IT and organisational skills. Candidates should be proficient with Outlook, Word, Excel, should have competent keyboard skills, and knowledge of a dental software package would be an advantage. Administrative support for Dental Officer, Dental Therapist and Dental Nurse, ensuring smooth running of clinics and/or dental administration offices. Be responsible for opening and closing of dental clinic premises. Provide general clerical support including typing correspondence and clinical letters, mail handling, stock control and photocopying. Maintain appropriate records, registry system (postal), and file correspondence and clinical records, ensuring compliance with the agreed record keeping systems of the Trust, including completion of NHS Dental Forms. Order and maintain stock, stationery and consumables. File records, clinical correspondence and radiographs. Take minutes for meetings as and when required to do so. Further information about the Trust and this role can be found on the Job Description and Person Specification document attached.
